title: The Plastic Bag Debate
text:
A good argumentative essay must do more than express an opinion. The writer needs a clear thesis, reliable evidence and logical reasoning. Many students forget that their readers may hold different beliefs, so they should address the strongest counterarguments as well.

Take the question of whether cities should ban plastic bags. Supporters point out that plastic bags take hundreds of years to break down and often end up in rivers and oceans. A persuasive essay on this topic would admit that some shops fear losing customers, and then explain why the environmental benefits still outweigh those concerns.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does a good argumentative essay need?
options: A clear thesis, reliable evidence and logical reasoning
A long list of famous quotations
Humorous stories about the writer's life

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, how long do plastic bags take to break down?
Why should a persuasive essay admit that some shops fear losing customers?
options: To show that it has considered the other side's concerns
To prove that shops are never affected by policies
To suggest that the writer supports plastic bags

questions.text: What can be inferred about the writer's view of the ban?
options: The writer thinks the environmental benefits are more important
The writer thinks shops should decide alone
The writer is neutral and has no opinion
The writer believes plastic bags are harmless

vocabulary.definition: the main claim that a writer argues for in an essay
arguments that oppose or challenge a position
able to convince someone to believe or do something
to be more important or valuable than something else

paragraph_translations: Um bom ensaio argumentativo precisa fazer mais do que expressar uma opinião. O autor precisa de uma tese clara, de evidências confiáveis e de raciocínio lógico. Muitos alunos esquecem que seus leitores podem ter crenças diferentes, por isso devem abordar também os contra-argumentos mais fortes.

Pense na questão de saber se as cidades deveriam proibir sacolas plásticas. Os defensores destacam que essas sacolas levam centenas de anos para se decompor e frequentemente acabam em rios e oceanos. Um ensaio persuasivo sobre o tema deveria admitir que algumas lojas temem perder clientes e, em seguida, explicar por que os benefícios ambientais ainda superam essas preocupações.
